overview: The oxidised and reduced forms of the same electron-carrier molecule used throughout cellular respiration.
genZNote: NAD+ is the empty electron shuttle waiting at the station. NADH is the same shuttle, now loaded with cargo (electrons).

aspects.label: Oxidised or Reduced?
aspects.valueA: The oxidised form — has not yet picked up electrons.
aspects.valueB: The reduced form — has accepted a hydride ion (2 electrons + 1 proton).

aspects.label: Role in Respiration
aspects.valueA: Acts as an electron acceptor during glycolysis, the Krebs cycle, and beta-oxidation.
aspects.valueB: Carries high-energy electrons to the electron transport chain to generate ATP.

aspects.label: Relative Energy Content
aspects.valueB: Higher energy form — its electrons drive ATP synthesis.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Each NADH that enters the electron transport chain yields roughly 2.5-3 ATP via oxidative phosphorylation.
overlay.memoryTrick: NAD+ picks up electrons to become NADH — the 'H' marks it's now carrying hydrogen/electrons.
overlay.commonMisconception: NAD+ and NADH are not two different molecules — they are the same coenzyme cycling between its oxidised and reduced states.
